subject.title: feat(config): use datetime suffix for config backup files instead of numeric rotation

question: Should a timestamped config-backup scheme preserve or convert existing numbered `.bak.N` files, or may it prune them on first post-upgrade cleanup?
rationale: Config backups may be the only rollback copies after a bad config write, and OpenClaw policy treats config recovery and migration behavior as compatibility-sensitive.

options.title: Preserve legacy recovery points
options.body: Require the linked PR or replacement to keep existing numbered backups through migration or convert them into the new bounded timestamped retention set without silent loss.

options.title: Prune legacy numbered backups
options.body: Accept a timestamp-only cleanup even if the first maintenance cycle after upgrade deletes existing `.bak.N` files.

options.title: Keep the numeric ring
options.body: Decline the naming change for now and keep the current five-slot numbered recovery model.

recommendation.title: Preserve legacy recovery points
recommendation.body: Require the linked PR or replacement to keep existing numbered backups through migration or convert them into the new bounded timestamped retention set without silent loss.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available routing signal combines config compatibility policy, the merged cleanup provenance, and backup-rotation test history.
